title: Build your own key-value database
description: Ashgrove Press keeps its stock counts in one file that Sefton's stock script writes again whole on every change, and twice the power went in the middle of a write and the file came back half empty. You write the shop a small database of its own on Node's file functions: keys and values, a log that only grows, records that hold any text and survive being cut short, compaction that swaps a new log in at one stroke, and batches that are all there or not at all, until the stock runs on it. By the end you know what a database does to keep what it was given when the program stops halfway.
